source.title: Minimum Array Changes to Make Differences Equal

teaching.hint: For one mirrored pair, how does its least cost vary with the chosen common difference?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: For each pair, a target difference costs zero at its current difference, one across a contiguous reachable range, and two otherwise; these costs can be aggregated over all targets.
solution_outline.approach: For every mirrored pair, derive its current difference and largest difference reachable by changing one endpoint. Add its cost contributions over target values `0..k` with range updates, sweep total cost, and take the minimum.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The accumulated range effects equal the exact sum of per-pair minimum changes for each candidate `X`.
solution_outline.correctness: Pairs are independent once `X` is fixed. A pair needs zero changes at its existing difference, one within its one-endpoint reach, and two for every other allowed target; the sweep checks every possible `X`.
solution_outline.pitfall: Only considering current pair differences, or using the wrong one-change reach, can miss the best target.

common_wrong_turns: Recompute every pair cost for every X
Pair i with i+n/2 rather than n−1−i
source_fidelity_notes: The mirrored pairing and replacement range are explicit; `X` lies in `[0,k]` because final values do.
